title: NTA clarifies Aadhaar and Class 10 name mismatch won't affect JEE Main 2027 candidature; NRI, OCI rules and Session 1 deadlines - Education Times

 News › News News › NTA clarifies Aadhaar and Class 10 name mismatch won't affect JEE Main 2027 candidature; NRI, OCI ru… NTA clarifies Aadhaar and Class 10 name mismatch won't affect JEE Main 2027 candidature; NRI, OCI rules and Session 1 deadlines
 Adhya Sarna Updated: Nov 16, 2026, 07:49 IST NTA issues clarification on JEE rules The National Testing Agency (NTA) has clarified that a difference between a candidate's name on the Aadhaar card and the Class 10 certificate will not affect their JEE Main 2027 candidature.
 The clarification forms part of a set of 48 frequently asked questions (FAQs) released by the agency on November 13 to address common queries about the engineering entrance examination.
 Rules for Aadhaar and Class 10 name mismatches
 According to NTA, candidates must enter their names in the JEE Main 2027 application form exactly as they appear on their Class 10 certificate or marksheet. Even if the name on the Aadhaar card differs, applicants are required to follow the Class 10 document while filling out the form. 
 The agency has stated that such a mismatch will not have any bearing on a candidate's candidature.
 Rules for NRI , OCI and foreign applicants
 Indian nationals, OCI cardholders and foreign nationals are eligible to apply for JEE Main 2027, and NRI and PIO candidates are also listed among eligible categories. NTA also conducts the examination at select centres outside India for NRI and foreign national candidates.
 On identity proof, NTA has allowed NRI candidates applying for Session 1 to use their passports as valid identity proof during registration. 
 The clarification followed a query from an NRI candidate who asked how applicants without an Aadhaar card, PAN card or driving licence could complete the process. Foreign nationals, including OCI cardholders, must upload a scanned non-Indian passport. Candidates studying outside India are advised not to assume that the options meant for students in India apply to them, and should check the information bulletin for provisions specific to their category.
 Key Session 1 deadlines
 Session 1 registration opened on October 24, 2026, and candidates can apply and pay the fee until November 22, 2026, up to 11:50 PM. Other key dates are as follows:
 Late registration: November 23 to November 26, 2026, with an additional late fee of ₹500.
 Application correction window: November 27 to November 29, 2026.
 Session 1 examination: Reportedly, the exam dates can be between January 20 and January 30, 2027.
 Session 2 registration: January 5 to February 3, 2027, up to 11:50 PM.
 Candidates are advised to confirm all dates on the official NTA website.
 The document released by NTA covers registration, DigiLocker, APAAR ID, eligibility, application correction, examination city selection, fee payment and examination-day guidelines. 
 It is intended to help candidates resolve routine doubts before submitting their applications.
 APAAR ID and DigiLocker
 NTA has confirmed that an APAAR ID is not mandatory for JEE Main 2027 registration, and candidates may complete their applications without providing it. The agency has also advised candidates to complete DigiLocker Re-KYC before registering. This will help retrieve their latest photograph for display on the application confirmation page. 
 Candidates who face difficulties with DigiLocker registration have been advised to retry using their own login credentials.
 Other key clarifications
 Category certificate: Candidates are not required to upload a category certificate during registration. They must, however, furnish the certificate number, date of issue and details of the issuing authority.
 Class 12 roll number: Students appearing for the Class 12 examination in 2026-27 may select the "Not Available" option if their roll number or registration number has not yet been issued.
 Application correction: NTA will provide a one-time correction facility for selected fields in the application form.
 Session 2 registration: Candidates wishing to appear in the April 2027 session must submit a separate application.
 Examination city: Candidates may select up to four preferred cities, subject to NTA's address-based conditions.
 Live photograph: Candidates may retake their live photograph multiple times if it is not accepted by the system.
 Improvement candidates: Students appearing in Class 12 improvement examinations must select the "Passed" option.
 Registration status
 JEE Main 2027 Session 1 registration is under way. According to the latest live update, around 7.8 lakh application forms had been submitted as of 2:13 AM IST on November 16, 2026.
 Advice to candidates
 Aspirants should read the complete set of 48 FAQs carefully before filling out their applications, as errors in personal details or document-related fields may lead to avoidable complications later. With the Session 1 deadline close, candidates should keep their Class 10 certificate, category certificate details, DigiLocker credentials and, for NRI, OCI and foreign applicants, a valid passport ready before beginning registration. The FAQs are available for download on the official NTA JEE Main website, which candidates should continue to monitor for further notices.
